commits.message:
fix(cells): cutCells walks once, so each character lands on one side (rich-segment-cvn6)

splitCells built its halves from two walks, cellFit from the left and
cellFitEnd from the right. Both take zero-width clusters, so one at the cut
landed in both halves ("hello­world" folded at width 5 printed the soft
hyphen twice), and where per-cluster widths outsum cellLen of the whole the
walks left a gap and dropped the characters in it.

cutCells (cells.ts, beside splitText) takes the left side with one cellFit,
and the right side is the rest of the text with the glyph the cut went
through, if any, blanked. cellColToCodeUnitOffset is now cellFitFrom from
the start rather than a second fit walk with its own zero-width rule, and
the fit walks count code units instead of building strings to measure.

fix(cells): every cell walk steps by grapheme cluster (rich-segment-cvn6)

cellFitFrom, cellStepFrom, splitAtCells and cellColToCodeUnitOffset still
walked code points, so chopCells counted 👍🏽 as 4 cells and 👨‍👩‍👧 as 6. Its
cuts drifted into the next wide glyph, and splitCells now blanks a glyph a
cut goes through, so fold dropped text: "👍🏽a漢" at width 2 printed
["👍🏽", "a ", " "], losing 漢.

All of them now walk clustersFrom, which steps one memoized segmentation with
Segments.containing so a caller stepping along one string stays linear
(chopCells on 1M chars: 107ms; slicing the tail per step took 5s).
cropToWidth was splitText's left side and is gone; setCellSize crops through
splitText.

fix(cells): split on grapheme clusters, the unit cellLen measures (rich-segment-cvn6)

splitText walked code points while cellLen measures grapheme clusters, so
the previous commit's overhang arithmetic went negative on any glyph built
from several code points: `new Segment("a⚠️b").splitCells(2)` threw
RangeError, and so did Console.print wrapping "warn ⚠️ ok ⚠️ done ⚠️ x" at
width 6 — a crash master did not have. ZWJ, skin-tone and combining-mark
glyphs left an orphaned tail on the right half.

splitCells now takes each half as cellFit/cellFitEnd's whole clusters padded
to its share of the cells, so neither pad can go negative and the right
half's anchor at `position` holds by construction. splitText's left side is
cellFit's, which fixes the same mismatch for cropLines, Dropdown and
TextInput.

fix(segment): a cut through a wide glyph splits it into two blank cells (rich-segment-cvn6)

Segment.splitCells padded the left half and kept a cut glyph whole on the
right, so the halves were one cell wider than the segment. Segment.divide
counted from the padded left half, so every section after a mid-glyph cut
was measured from the wrong column — and WidgetApp paints overlays through
divide, so an overlay ending halfway through a CJK glyph widened the row
under it by a cell ("abc字漢字" in an 8-cell row).

The halves are now exactly `position` and `len - position` cells, a cut
glyph leaving a space on each side — the reference's split_cells. The
right half's anchor shift is therefore just `position`.

fix(rich-explore): each coverage item starts its own row (rich-explore-demo-fgln) (#273)

* fix(rich-explore): each coverage item starts its own row (rich-explore-demo-fgln)

The coverage view built its Group items as RichText with end "", which
leaves the line open as Rich's Text does, so the Group drew the next item
on the same row — 14 rows wider than 80 cells. The items end their lines
now, and the Emoji, a line fragment as in Rich, sits in a grid row beside
its label. The test compares the view's row count with the sum of its
items' rows, which catches a join too short to overflow the width.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(rich-explore): each coverage item ends its own line, checked per item (rich-explore-demo-fgln)

The row-sum check re-derived Group's arithmetic from hand-copied render
options and missed an open item in the last position. Each item is now
rendered alone under the options the frame was drawn with, and must draw
nothing or end with a newline. The view also shows chopCells' array and
setCellSize's result instead of discarding one and stringifying the other.
